audience: Developers, technical SEOs, and documentation/dev-tool teams evaluating whether to adopt an emerging AI web standard

questions.question: What exactly is llms.txt and who created it?
questions.answer_summary: llms.txt is a plain Markdown file placed at a site's root (e.g. /llms.txt) proposed by Jeremy Howard of Answer.AI/fast.ai in September 2024 to give AI systems a curated, one-line-description index of a site's most important content, framed as 'robots.txt for the AI era.'

questions.question: Is llms.txt an official, ratified web standard?
questions.answer_summary: No — it remains a proposed community standard. Neither the IETF nor W3C has ratified it, and adoption is driven by individual companies (Anthropic docs, Vercel, Stripe, Answer.AI) rather than a formal body.

questions.question: Do OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Perplexity actually read and use llms.txt when crawling or answering?
questions.answer_summary: As of the discussion, none of the major AI providers has publicly confirmed that their production crawlers or answer systems consume llms.txt normatively; a Hacker News thread explicitly asks 'Is LLMs.txt a REAL thing now?' reflecting this uncertainty.

questions.question: What is the difference between llms.txt and llms-full.txt?
questions.answer_summary: llms.txt is a streamlined navigation index of a site's key pages with short descriptions, while llms-full.txt is a comprehensive file containing the full documentation content in one place.

questions.question: Does llms.txt block or restrict AI crawlers the way robots.txt does?
questions.answer_summary: No — it is a discovery/navigation aid, not an access-control mechanism; it cannot prevent any AI system from reading a site the way robots.txt directives are intended to restrict crawler behavior.

questions.question: Is it worth the time to create an llms.txt file in 2026?
questions.answer_summary: Community sentiment described it as low-cost and largely harmless but not a meaningful visibility lever; one cited large-scale study claims a majority of these files go unread, and most of what does read them isn't even an AI system.

questions.question: Does llms.txt help with live AI search citations (e.g. being cited by ChatGPT search) or only with AI coding/dev tools reading documentation?
questions.answer_summary: The strongest confirmed real-world use case is developer tooling — AI coding assistants fetching documentation more efficiently — rather than influencing live AI search answer citations, where its effect is unconfirmed.

questions.question: What has Google said about llms.txt?
questions.answer_summary: Google's public position, as characterized in industry coverage, is that creating an llms.txt file will neither harm nor help a site's visibility.
